How a Term's Block Moves Along Four Directions

Source: R/block_deriv4.R
term_block_deriv4.Rd

Returns the fourth derivative of a term's block along four directions, one entry per observation and column of the block, the companion of term_block_deriv3() at the next order.

Usage

term_block_deriv4(term, coef = NULL, v, u, s, r, ...)

Arguments

term

A built term.

coef

The coefficients, one per coefficient of the term, or NULL for the coefficients that the term carries.

v, u, s, r

Numeric vectors as long as the term's coefficients.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A numeric matrix, one row per observation and one column per coefficient of the term.

Details

The base method returns zeros. For nl() the entry is the fifth derivative of the predictor along the column and the four directions, written out over the 52 partitions of the five: grouped by the block that holds the column, of size five (one partition), four (four), three (six with the other two directions together and six with them apart), two (four choices, each with the other three directions in one block, in a pair and a single in three ways, or apart) and one (the fifteen partitions of the four directions). Each block of a partition carries the derivative of one inverse link to its size and each partition the derivative of \(f\) to its number of blocks. A parameter whose development moves is rejected, as in term_block_deriv3(). For scs() and scte() the entry is \(G_{il}W_{ij}b^{(5)}(\gamma_j)\,v_ju_js_jr_j\), as in term_block_deriv3() one order more.

A class whose block moves with its coefficients must implement its own method of this generic, because the zeros of the base method are wrong for such a block. statmodels7 reads this generic in the exact derivatives of an outer criterion and uses those derivatives only for a class with a method of its own; for any other class it computes them by differences. It recognizes a method of its own by comparing the method registered for the class with the base method, so a class that registers the base method itself under its own name is treated as having a method of its own, and the zeros enter the derivatives.

See also

term_block_deriv3()

Examples

dd <- data.frame(x = seq(0.2, 3, length.out = 20))
dd$y <- 2 * exp(-1.3 * dd$x)
b <- term_build(nl(~ a * exp(-r * x), start = list(a = 2, r = 1.3)), dd)
dim(term_block_deriv4(b, v = c(1, 0), u = c(0, 1), s = c(1, 1),
                      r = c(1, -1)))
#> [1] 20  2
